eligibility.quote:
The NaN value should be converted to a NaN in python.

The [BatteryState](https://github.com/ros2/common_interfaces/blob/b7e2ad503e1648468b1dc766c43aac12cc9aee5a/sensor_msgs/msg/BatteryState.msg) message, for example, uses NaNs to flag values that are not measured.

notes: Issue #848 ("pybind11 error during subscription take_message() when message has NaN value") documents that an rclpy subscriber crashes with "make_tuple(): unable to convert argument of type 'object' to Python object" when a NaN value is published on /nan. I read the issue body, the thread (fujitatomoya: "https://github.com/ros2/rosidl_python/pull/167 can fix this problem."; clalancette: "Yes, good call. I'm actually going to close this one as a duplicate, since it is already fixed in Rolling..."), rosidl_python PR #167 ("Allow NaN values to pass floating point bounds check.", which changes the generated assertion from "value >= -bound and value <= bound" to "not (value < -bound or value > bound) or math.isinf(value)"), and rosidl_python #162 (quoted above). NaN/inf are valid values for the declared float types (BatteryState uses NaN to flag unmeasured values), so the value crossing the topic boundary is not wrong; the defect is the generated Python setter rejecting a valid value plus rclpy's unchecked error path, both inside the subscribing process. E2 stops at step 2 (internal), which is correct. Loudness/resolution correctly null.
